Pete Fiutak Wed, October 7, 2026 at 4:58 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's amazing how fast two weeks can change things. Louisville appeared to be ready to make a charge with a close loss to Ole Miss, a great 41-31 win over SMU, and winnable games coming up. A 30-27 loss to Wake Forest and a 31-28 loss to NC State later, and now the Cardinals have to win to stay alive in the ACC race. Florida State was done. Head coach Mike Norvell was all but fired, and then everything flipped. The Seminoles tuned up against Central Arkansas, and then stunned Virginia 38-7. Win this, and the season narrative totally changes. Florida State vs Louisville Quick Hits Florida State is on the road for four games in the next five, with a trip to Miami up next before hosting Clemson. Louisville goes to Syracuse next to start a run of three road games in four dates. Before the last meeting in the 2023 ACC Championship, the two teams split the previous ten games. How To Watch Florida State vs Louisville Date: Friday, October 9, 2026 Game Time: 7:00 PM ET TV: ESPN Location: L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium, Louisville, KY – Week 6 Schedule & Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predictions For Every Remaining Game – CFN Expert Picks: Week 6 Why Florida State Will Win So what did Florida State do against Virginia to generate all of this excitement? The defense pitched one of its best games in a long time, considering the circumstances, holding the Cavalier passing game in check with a monstrous day from the pass rush. The Noles generated ten sacks and 12 tackles for loss. The relentless pressure should continue against a Louisville offensive front that's having a problem keeping teams out of the backfield. Why Louisville Will Win Can Florida State show up on the road? It's not quite fair to dog the Noles for losing at Alabama, but the program has lost 13 straight games outside of Tallahassee, going back to the win over Florida late in 2023. Louisville has to take a deep breath after the NC State loss. It played well. The ground game was great, quarterback Lincoln Kienholz was fine on his dinged up ankle, and everything was fine outside of three lost fumbles. Florida State hasn't forced a takeaway in a month. Florida State vs Louisville Prediction, Betting Lines Florida State isn't awful. The pieces are there – the ground game is solid, and look out if that pass rush keeps on rolling – but they have a hard time always fitting together. The Seminoles will crank up plenty of yards and points – the Louisville defense isn't anything special – but the offense will stall a few too many times, and the Cardinals will find their offensive scoring punch after two straight disappointments. The dual-threat shredded the Demon Deacons with 324 passing yards and a touchdown, while also crossing the end zone twice on running plays. Yet his efforts weren’t enough to topple Wake Forest. All the more reason why this ACC showdown is pivotal for them to catapult back into the conference title game conversation. Louisville already has absorbed two losses this season, starting with the opening defeat at the hands of Ole Miss. The Cards are now the eighth-best team in the ACC, placing them in the middle of the pack. Fortunately for Louisville the schedule lightens up from here starting with NC State. Only No. 24 Kentucky is the last nationally-ranked foe the Cardinals must face, which isn’t until Nov. 28. UL still has contests against teams with a nebulous coaching future: Florida State, Syracuse and North Carolina. But again, head coach Jeff Brohm and the Cards must rebound quick against the Wolfpack before their season folds. Like ClutchPoints’ content? Be sure to follow us. picks.headline: Adam Carriker's Nebraska Football vs. Indiana Preview & Prediction
picks.blurb: Adam Carriker's Nebraska Football vs. Indiana Preview & Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska is getting ready for a huge Big Ten matchup against Indiana, and Adam Carriker breaks down what the Huskers have to do if they want to pull off the upset and earn some serious respect. This is one of those games that can change the way people look at a team. Nebraska has put together a strong start, but now the Huskers get a chance to prove it against a ranked Indiana team led by Curt Cignetti. Indiana has been one of the best teams in the Big Ten, and this game will give Matt Rhule’s team a chance to show how far it has come. Carriker starts by looking back at the history between Nebraska and Indiana; he then shifts to Nebraska’s offense and quarterback Anthony Colandrea. If Nebraska is going to win this game, Colandrea will need to have a big day. He has to make smart decisions, take care of the football, and make plays with both his arm and his legs. Carriker also compares Colandrea to Indiana’s quarterback Josh Hoover and talks about why Nebraska needs to put pressure on Hoover and force him into mistakes. The Huskers’ pass catchers are another major part of the matchup. Nebraska has playmakers who can make a difference, and Carriker takes a closer look at players like Kwazi Gilmer and how they match up with Indiana’s defense. On the other side of the ball, Nebraska’s defense could be one of the biggest factors in the game. Rob Aurich and the Nebraska defense will need to be at their best, especially on third down. Indiana has talented receivers, solid running backs, and an offense that can hurt teams in several different ways. Nebraska cannot afford to give up easy conversions or big plays. One of the biggest topics in the episode is penalties. Nebraska had 16 penalties last week while Indiana had zero. That is a massive difference, and Carriker makes it clear that Nebraska cannot expect to beat a ranked team if it keeps hurting itself. Cleaning up the penalties is one of his biggest keys to the game. Carriker wraps up the show by laying out five keys for Nebraska: limit penalties, stop the run, play four full quarters, run the football, and limit big plays. None of those things are complicated, but Nebraska has to do all five if it wants to compete and win. The Huskers also need to be ready for a physical game. Carriker talks about trading blows with Indiana and matching the Hoosiers for all four quarters. This cannot be a game where Nebraska plays well for two or three quarters and then fades late. The second half will be huge. Carriker also throws in a little extra motivation with a beard bet if Nebraska wins. At the end of the show, he gives his final score prediction: Indiana 27, Nebraska 24. He sees it as a close game, but Nebraska will need a big performance from Colandrea, a strong game from the defense, and much cleaner football to pull off the upset. He was twice named first-team All-Big 12, leading the conference in sacks and winning the Big 12 Defensive Lineman of the Year award his senior season, along with several other awards, including finishing with All-America honors, in addition to being named to the Big 12 Commissioner’s Academic Honor Roll three times. He’s also been named to Nebraska’s All-Century Team, voted The Best Husker Defensive End since the start of the new millennium, and has been inducted into the Nebraska Football Hall of Fame. Adam went on to play eight years as a Defensive Lineman in the NFL with the St. Louis Rams and Washington Redskins. He was drafted in the 1st round, winning Rams Rookie of the Year; he’s the only Ram in franchise history to start all 16 games as a rookie. He also won the Strongest Redskin award multiple times during his career in the NFL. Since retiring, he’s experienced great success in the business world and has also appeared multiple times on National Television and Radio Shows, and currently hosts his highly popular show, the Carriker Chronicles, aka, the People’s Show, which has been viewed by millions! That won't be good enough against the Huskers' biggest test yet: the undefeated, defending national champions from Indiana . Rob Aurich knows it, too, and the Huskers' defensive coordinator says Saturday's contest will be decided by how well NU handles the little things, from players doing their jobs to tackling at a high level. Indiana's Turbo Richard runs for a touchdown against Western Kentucky. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Hoosiers' offense ranks 14th nationally, averaging 489.6 yards and 44.2 points per game. Aurich said some simple qualities will be key to slowing Indiana down. “Play style, speed, and physicality,” Aurich told reporters Tuesday. “Run to the ball. I thought two weeks ago we ran to the ball harder than we did last week. I was disappointed in that. I want people to talk about our defense as the hardest-playing group in the country. So, we’ve got to play extremely hard.” “The backs have a high break tackle ratio,” he continued. “We’ve got to tackle their backs at an elite level, which is something we’re going to work on today.” Anthony Jones Jr. makes a tackle against Michigan State. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Huskers allowed several explosive plays against the Terrapins last week, which is a major concern heading into a matchup against the likes of Indiana. Aurich knows Nebraska won't be able to completely shut the Hoosiers down. But he does want to see the Huskers continue to bow up in the red zone, something they've been doing at a high level. Aurich mentioned Dwayne McDougle's game-changing 81-yard pick-six in the second quarter against Maryland. “He looked at that look all week, and so he had an opportunity to execute something he’s done" Aurich said. "I’ve been extremely pleased with our guys’ ability to toughen up in some big moments.” “I was really proud with how we survived that first half when things were a little noisy,” he continued. “I was really, really pleased with how they responded and we toughened up. (Photo by Nathanial George/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images thehooch36 Mon, October 5, 2026 at 1:29 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads College Football can be odd. One minute, you're winning your conference opener on the road 31-13. The next minute, you're winning you're conference home opener 48-25. You don't look particularly great in either contest, but you cover the spread, hold up your end of the bargain, and sit 5-0 to start the year for the first time since 2016. That's the story of the Nebraska Cornhuskers. LINCOLN, NE - OCTOBER 3: Nebraska defensive back Jeremiah Charles (25) celebrates after blocking a punt in the first quarter of the game between the Maryland Terrapins and the Nebraska Cornhuskers on October 3, 2026, at Memorial Stadium in Lincoln, NE. (Photo by Nathanial George/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Nebraska took care of the Maryland Terrapins, albeit with one of the more dysfunctional beginnings to a game you'll see. A penalty on a (nearly) blocked punt that extended Maryland's drive, resulting in a field goal. Then after a three-and-out, an actual blocked punt that resulted in a Mekhi Nelson touchdown, his first of two in the game. Nebraska trained as much as 16-7, but still led 28-23 heading into halftime. The third quarter was a checkers match of moving a piece at a time, far away from your opponent. But the Huskers scored two seconds into the fourth quarter, and added two more touchdowns before the game ended. Meanwhile, the Nebraska defense held the Terps scoreless and relatively impotent after the 8:54 mark of the second quarter. Now it is time for the Huskers' biggest (and some may say first true) test of the season when the defending national champion Indiana Hoosiers make their way to Lincoln for Fox's Big Noon Kickoff. Curt Cignetti has his team in the top ten (top five in the Coaches' Poll), and even though there's no Fernando Mendoza, the Hoosiers are the only other team in the Bin ten to be undefeated. They have only been threatened once this year, when the Northwestern Wildcats of all teams gave them a scare, as the Hoosiers won that September 25 contest 29-23 at home. Indiana handled Rutgers this past weekend, and they mowed through their non-conference opponents (North Texas, Howard, and Western Kentucky) on easy mode. away.headline: Indiana Availability Report: Lee Beebe's Status and Who's Out vs Rutgers
away.blurb: Indiana Availability Report: Lee Beebe's Status and Who's Out vs Rutgers Skip to main content SI.COM Indiana could be without its leading rusher Saturday night when the Hoosiers take on Rutgers, with running back Lee Beebe Jr. listed as a game-time decision, per the Big Ten's availability report . Beebe, who rushed for 203 yards in Indiana's win over Northwestern last week, was a midweek addition to the availability report. His status headlines an otherwise encouraging final injury update for the Hoosiers, who had three players removed from the report ahead of their first road test of the season. Richard was listed as probable Friday before being removed from Saturday's report, putting him in line to handle the bulk of Indiana's rushing workload should Beebe be unable to go. Cuono, a second-year depth running back with 11 carries for 45 yards this season, would likely serve as Richard's primary backup in that scenario. True freshman Jayreon Campbell, who has rushed six times for 43 yards in limited action, is also available. Khobie Martin, meanwhile, remains out for the fourth consecutive game as he continues recovering from a forearm injury he suffered in Indiana's season opener against North Texas. Martin is expected to return around the midway point of the season. Indiana enters Saturday with a rushing attack ranked among the nation's top 10, although Beebe's potential absence would leave the Hoosiers without one of their most productive offensive weapons. Linebacker Rolijah Hardy, who was listed as probable Friday after suffering an injury late in his eight-tackle performance against Northwestern, was also removed from Saturday's availability report and is expected to play. A.J. Harris, Daniel Ndukwe among those ruled out Defensive end Daniel Ndukwe is also out, marking his first absence of the season. Ndukwe ranks second on the team with 4.5 tackles for loss, including 1.5 against Northwestern last week. Indiana still has considerable depth at edge, with Stephen Daley, Kellan Wyatt, Tobi Osunsanmi, Chiddi Obiazor and Josh Burnham available to help absorb his absence. Elsewhere, cornerback Carson Williams and wide receiver Lebron Bond remain out for the third and fourth consecutive games, respectively. Indiana and Rutgers are scheduled to kick off at 8 p.m. ET. home.headline: Nebraska Upgrades Jamal Rule and Jacory Barney on Latest Availability Report; Mekhi Nelson Unchanged
home.blurb: Rule was labeled as doubtful in NU's initial availability report Wednesday. He remained there Thursday before moving up to questionable Friday. His return would bolster a running back room with an alarmingly low amount of career production. After being upgraded from questionable to probable, he appears set to return against the Terps. That would give the Huskers a key piece in both their passing and return games. If he sits this one out, more catches could be in store for Quinn Clark and Keelan Smith. Isaiah Mozee and Andrew Marshall are options as punt returners. The surprising news came Thursday when junior running back Mekhi Nelson was added to the availability report as questionable. That status stayed the same on Friday. Nelson's availability would provide a significant boost for the Huskers on the ground against Maryland. With Jamal Rule also questionable, NU could enter Saturday's contest without their two most productive backs. Isaiah Mozee, listed as a co-No. 1 on the depth chart with Rule and Nelson, has 31 carries for 149 yards this season, plus three receptions for 37 yards. Backups Kwinten Ives, Vincent Genatone and Conor Booth have combined for 10 carries for 49 yards and three receptions for 38 yards. Friday's reports from Maryland and Nebraska | Big Ten Conference Others listed on the report include Rex Guthrie and Brendan Black as probable. Both players have remained that way since Wednesday. Both players have remained that way since Wednesday. Bryson Webber and Tanner Terch have been upgraded from questionable to probable since the initial report was released. Larry Miles, Kahmir Prescott, Gage Stenger, Jase Reynolds, Jacob Bower, and Gabe Moore have yet to see the field this season for the Big Red. For the most part, potentially excluding Moore, those players will remain listed as out for the rest of the year. Junior tight end Carter Nelson suffered an injury in the second half of the Huskers' win over North Dakota and left the field appearing to be in severe pain. He has been listed as out on every report since then. picks.blurb: West Virginia football expert previews the Arizona Wildcats game, makes a score prediction | Arizona Desert Swarm Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo An Arizona Wildcats Community Arizona Desert Swarm October 7, 2026 Arizona Desert Swarm Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Arizona Basketball Arizona Football Arizona Softball Arizona Recruiting Arizona Soccer Arizona Volleyball Arizona Baseball Arizona Gymnastics Arizona in the Pros Betting FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Arizona Football Odds Arizona Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Arizona Basketball Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Arizona Football RichRod Week! It’s not just Game Week, it’s RichRod Game Week! Arizona’s first trip to West Virginia will see it face off against former head coach Rich Rodriguez , who is back with the Mountaineers for a second go-around. Rodriguez coached there from 2001-07 before going to Michigan for three years and then spending 2012-17 with the Wildcats. The current West Virginia team is on a 2-game skid, losing a 45-42 shootout at Iowa State last weekend after falling at home to Oklahoma State in its Big 12 opener. To better understand RichRod’s squad, we reached out to Dillon Clark of SB Nation sister site The Smoking Musket for some insight and a score prediction. Below are his impressive answers to our mediocre questions: AZ Desert Swarm: West Virginia went 3-0 in nonconference play, including an impressive win over Virginia, but then has lost both conference games. What have been the main contributing factors to the backslide? Dillon Clark: “There has been a significant increase in competition in Big 12 play compared to our nonconference schedule. The win against Virginia looked good at the time because they were ranked, but after their performance against Florida State last week I don’t think they are going to be anywhere near the top of the ACC again. Our defense hasn’t looked great all year but the wheels have come completely off in the last two games. We have given up over 1,200 yards of total offense in the last two games which equates to about 3/4 of a mile if you were wondering.” It’s to no one’s surprise in Wildcat Nation that a RichRod-coached team is running the ball well, but this production seems to be at another level. What’s been the key to the rushing success, and how do you think Arizona’s defense will try to neutralize this? “We spent a ton of money in the portal on a quarterback, running back and several offensive linemen. Michael Hawkins Jr. has exceeded expectations at the quarterback position for us averaging over 100 yards per game on the ground 6.2 yards per carry. Many of his best runs are coming off of pass plays that would have resulted in a sack or throw away for most other QBs so when you turn those negative plays into big positives it really shows up on the stat sheet. One of the biggest surprises to me has been his elusiveness in the red zone and the ability to make people miss. I knew he was fast, I didn’t realize how shifty he is. Cam Cook has also produced at a high level in the RB position. He is such a tough runner. His yards after contact and broken tackles are what really sets him apart. Even though he isn’t what I would call fast, he has consistently popped big runs. He gets stronger as the game goes on and the majority of his yardage has come in the second half of games.” Quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr. is tied for the FBS lead with 11 rushing touchdowns, but how is he as a passer? Would you trust him if he had to be one-dimensional in this way? “I think it’s fair to call Michael Hawkins Jr. a streaky passer. The last three games he has started out looking a bit shaky in the pass game with off target throws. In two of the three he eventually settled in and made plays with his arm. The completion percentage against Iowa State was a bit lower than you like, but he did have a couple drops and throw aways in there. I have confidence in him as a passer, my bigger question is can our receivers get open consistently in a situation where we have to throw the ball, and can we establish an intermediate passing game? It feels like our passing game at times this year has been all or nothing. The drive-extending, possession-style passing game has not been sharp. I don’t blame that on Michael Hawkins as much as I do on play calling and scheme. I have a hard time seeing anyone making him purely one dimensional as a passer this year. Teams may shut down our traditional running game, but we have seen teams put multiple spies on him in the past few weeks and he is still escaping the pocket for chunk yardage.” The Mountaineers’ defensive numbers are not good, ranking last in the Big 12 in almost every category. Is this a talent issue, a problem with the scheme, or both? “In order to be as bad as we have been, it has to be all of the above right? Our tackling is bad. Missed assignments on nearly every possession.We can’t get pressure on the quarterback. When we are in the right place we end up with a pass interference penalty. It’s rough all around. There has been a lot of talk on if Zac Alley’s reputation as a sort of ‘mad scientist’ on defense could be part of the problem. It’s really hard to argue against that when you see us consistently confused on pre-snap alignments. The biggest concern is that we are struggling in every aspect. Scoring defense, rushing defense, pass defense, total yardage, it doesn’t matter which stat you look at, we are at or near the bottom. The only hope is that potentially our two best defenders just became eligible last week. Jacorey Thomas and Jason Chambers should help plug some holes in what has been a leaky secondary. There is only one way for us to go from here.” How has the second coming of RichRod been so far in your estimation? Have there been any classic moments in terms of his antics? “After the Virginia win in Week 3 the vibes around the WVU fan base were as high as I’ve seen them in a very long time. That game brought back a lot of great memories from Rich Rod’s first tenure here and it felt like the sky was the limit. The last two weeks have put a damper on the mood though the fact that the offense has been producing at a high level still does take some of the blame off of him. The Rich Rod offense is back and it’s humming, but how did he not see this coming with the defense? There was definitely a group of the fanbase that didn’t want him back, and those voices are getting louder with each loss. I think he has shown enough so far that the majority of the fan base still believes he can get this right. We love that he holds players accountable in the moment, and it gives us hope that he can turn this thing around.” Prediction time. Does Arizona beat its former coach and get a big conference road win or do the Mountaineers hold serve at home? Give us a score prediction. “We have the worst defense in the Big 12. You have one of the best offenses. We are coming off of two straight brutal conference losses. You are coming off of a dominant win against a previously undefeated Cincinnati team. In other words, we have you right where we want you. 45-31 Mountaineers get back on track at home.” Download the new SB Nation app All of your communities in one place. Former Oklahoma, Houston and Tarleton State player Cody Jackson erupted for 160 receiving yards in the Cyclones’ momentum swing-filled 45-42 triumph over West Virginia at Jack Trice Stadium. Oct 3, 2026 Updated Oct 3, 2026 AMES — Cody Jackson transferred to Iowa State last winter in search of his fourth fresh start. The talented transfer wide receiver found it, but catches proved tough to come by. Until Saturday, when the former Oklahoma, Houston and Tarleton State player erupted for 160 receiving yards in the Cyclones’ momentum swing-filled 45-42 triumph over West Virginia at Jack Trice Stadium. “I trusted in God, number one, and trusted in my coaches (and) my teammates,” said Jackson, who didn’t record a catch in ISU’s first two games, but now has 12 receptions in the past two games. “Not having my head down. Keeping my head high. Keeping a smile on my face every day and coming in and working at practice.” Jackson’s first grab on Saturday for the Cyclones (3-2, 1-1 Big 12) turned into a 46-yard touchdown on a halfback toss from Aiden Flora. His other seven receptions against the Mountaineers (3-3, 0-2) came during a tense second half, and many fueled three straight scoring drives that helped ISU preserve the win. “He did a great job finding open windows and attacking the ball in the air,” Cyclones quarterback Jaylen Raynor said. Jackson notched 92 yards after the catch and often adjusted his routes as Raynor improvised amid amped up West Virginia pressure. His 43-yard catch on third-and-six early in the fourth quarter set up Kyle Konrardy’s 35-yard field goal that gave ISU a 31-28 lead. And Jackson’s 15-yard grab on the Cyclones’ final scoring drive ended in one of Flora’s three rushing touchdowns. Flora’s now averaging 8.1 yards per carry and has rushed for 600 yards and six touchdowns. “(He’s) a great leader,” Jackson said. “He can do everything, like you could see. away.source: Tulane Green Wave On SI on MSN
away.blurb: "We're at a point where we're going into conference play and we know we've got to play better," Hall told us at his weekly media conference. "We've not played our best yet. That's a negative, but also a positive that our best is still out there. You should get better as the season goes on....We feel like we're a much better football team right now than we were last time we talked to you (two weeks ago)," Expect the highly anticipated return of last year's breakout running back Jamauri McClure . The then-freshman sensation rushed for 540-yards, though really being used from about the midway point in the year on. He averaged 6.5-yards every time he touched the ball in 2025. McClure was injured during Fall practice getting surgery on his left foot to repair damage done. He's been sidelined all this year, with the Wave targeting the American opener as his season debut. Receiver Zycarl Lewis , who was hurt during the Duke game, is set to return as well, recovering from a leg injury. Though Hall listed both tight end Ty Thompson and linebacker Chris Rodgers as doubtful for Saturday, fans should not plan on either of them contributing this weekend. Thompson is nursing a leg injury that has forced him to miss extended time, and Rodgers has a foot injury that is putting the star backer on the sidelines for the foreseeable future. The Tulane football team opens the defense of its American Conference 2025 championship on Saturday with a trip to West Point to visit the United States Military Academy. Kickoff from Michie Stadium is set for 11:00 a.m. CT and can be seen on the CBS Sports Network. After a bye week to rest up and prepare, Green Wave head coach Will Hall is feeling good about his squad's preparedness. "The advantages of when our bye week fell is it is right smack dab in the middle of our season," Hall shared Tuesday. "We had five weeks of fall camp, then four games. That's nine weeks. Now we've got a bye week and eight games left. So, it's right in the middle. It is right before conference play and it's right before we play an option team. I think those are advantages The league opener is like a new season for Hall and his team, as they get ready for what is essentially a restart to their season. "We know how important it is to get off on the right foot and be 1-0 in conference play," Hall said Tuesday, "so our young men are taking that very seriously. But also we all want to play (well) for us and I want us to play (well) for our players. I want our players to play better, so in turn they get more touches and get more accolades for themselves and they get the the harvest for all the work they've put in. You can see it. You can feel it, and I anticipate us playing well." away.headline: Return of Jamauri McClure Brings Major Boost to Tulane Offense
away.blurb: Return of Jamauri McClure Brings Major Boost to Tulane Offense - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Return of Jamauri McClure Brings Major Boost to Tulane Offense As they practiced on Tuesday for game prep coming off their bye week, Green Wave running back Jamauri McClure was a sight for sore eyes out there, participating in team drills without a non-contact jersey for the first time since he went down with a fractured foot in fall camp. This year's room looks a lot different in comparison. Maurice Turner is playing his best football right now. Jaylin Lucas has gotten some work out in space a bit more this week of prep. Johnnie Daniels has shown that he can throw a killer block as much as he can shoot through a gap. However, the return of McClure is what fans have been clamoring for since the news first got out that he was hurt. Now that he's had ample time to recover, his return should be a major boost for a Tulane offense looking to make the most out of and stretch out what should be expected to be limited possessions against the Army Black Knights Saturday. Messi's Argentina farewell (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Maddy Hudak Tue, October 6, 2026 at 8:33 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The best ability is often availability, and the Tulane Green Wave certainly have some good news on that front ahead of American conference play. But while head coach Will Hall told media members on Tuesday that he and the team feel that they're a better football team than when we last talked to and saw them last two weeks back, they have a lot to prove on the road to kick off their conference slate. An essential thing they're looking for is an identity on offense. Well, a lot of that can be solved by a strong rush attack that McClure instantaneously boosts. When McClure started taking over the starting running back job towards the end of the year last season, it was clear that he had a different gear and set of traits than what we were seeing from that room. Further good news on that front is that nothing appears to be up with Turner, who ended up limping a bit at the end of his 74-yard touchdown run against the Southern Miss Golden Eagles, as he also was practicing in full with no non-contact jersey. But the true finesse of that room lies with McClure. Another major returnee was wide receiver Zycarl Lewis, who got injured during the season opener against the Duke Blue Devils and hasn't practiced or played since. He was also not in a non-contact jersey on the practice field Tuesday. McClure averaged an impressive 6.5 yards per carry last season. The redshirt sophomore had eight total carries until Week 12 of last year against the FAU Owls. In the final five games of the season, he added 75 touches for 83 total carries for 540 yards and two touchdowns.

away.headline: Army football seeks bounce back in return to home action vs. Tulane
away.blurb: News Sports Life Opinion Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals COLLEGE Army football seeks bounce back in return to home action vs. Tulane Ken McMillan Middletown Times Herald- Record Updated Oct. 6, 2026, 9:47 a.m. ET In the end, Army's 21-19 loss at Louisiana Tech on Saturday night was just a non-conference game and didn't affect the American Conference standings. However, the Black Knights are having trouble building on positives. "It's very hard to play perfect,'' said Monken, who also points out the margin for error is slim for his West Point teams. "We're going to strive to it.'' Monken pointed out that Army had too many missed assignments, played with poor fundamentals at times and didn't help themselves with six penalties, but he's not given up on the squad. A dominant win over Bryant in the opener, followed by a crushing late loss at home to South Florida. A tough road win over Temple, followed by a stumbling loss as a small favorite at Louisiana Tech , dropping the Black Knights to 2-2. "We're not going to let this game kind of derail our season,'' said senior center and co-captain Brady Small. "We're going to go back, we're going to watch some film, we're going to learn and get ready for Tulane, another conference game. So just use this as fuel to the fire to get us a win at home.'' Army is a three-point favorite over Tulane for Saturday's noon ET start. Army is 1-1 in American action, and needs a win vs. the Green Wave to stay in contact with the 1-0 leaders: Florida Atlantic (4-1 overall), Memphis (4-1), Texas San Antonio (4-1), Alabama Birmingham (3-2) and North Texas (3-2). Army will face FAU and Memphis but not the other three this season. "Honestly, we've just got to attack the adversity at hand,'' said back Samari Howard. "We can't let this be a lull in our preparation. Overall, we've got to come together as a collective and tackle the adversity and get ready for the next week and the week after that.'' "I don't believe anybody loses momentum unless they stop believing,'' head coach Jeff Monken said. "And I don't think our guys will stop believing. ... If we allow it to derail us, then shame on us. Weve got to learn from it, and each game is independent of the last one. I don't think we allowed last week (win over Temple) to linger into this week. We weren't patting ourselves on the back for such a great job.'' Monken always reminds people that winning college football games is hard. "I love our team,'' he said. "They're tough as nails. They compete, and we played all the way to the end tonight.'' West Point and New Orleans are separated by more than 1,300 miles, but the football programs at Army and Tulane remain very familiar. The Green Wave have a long history with the Black Knights, dating back to 1953 when the two schools battled to a scoreless draw. Next to service academy rivals Navy and Air Force, Army and Tulane have met quite often, 21 times since 1996. Tulane was a founding member of Conference USA in 199

Photo By - Reuters Connect. Texas defensive end Colin Simmons (1) celebrates with the Golden Hat following the Red River Rivalry. One of college football's best-known rivalries returns for its 122nd edition in Week 6, as Texas and Oklahoma meet at the Cotton Bowl in Dallas at 3:30 p.m. ET (ABC), with the Texas State Fair taking place right outside. The Texas vs. Oklahoma rivalry , better known as the Red River Rivalry, has been played every season since 1929, with these two storied programs often blocking each other from winning a conference championship or, in modern times, reaching the College Football Playoff. Texas is the favorite and has won Red River in three of the last four years, making it a popular pick among college football analysts . Texas vs Oklahoma 2026 preview Steve Sarkisian (52-20) Head coach (record with school) Brent Venables (34-22) SP+ special teams Texas vs Oklahoma odds Texas vs Oklahoma prediction The Red River Rivalry hasn't been kind to Oklahoma head coach Brent Venables. Since he took over the Sooners in 2022, he's 1-3 straight up and ATS against Texas . In those three wins for Steve Sarkisian, the Longhorns beat Venables' Sooners by an average of 32.3 points. That includes a 49-0 win in 2022, the third-largest blowout in the Red River Rivalry history. Even last year, when Oklahoma made the College Football Playoff and Texas didn't, the Longhorns beat the Sooners, 23-6. That was due in large part to a poor performance from ohn Mateer , who led Oklahoma to just 258 total yards while throwing three interceptions and accounting for six turnover-worthy plays. This year shouldn't be much different, with Mateer back behind center and ranking top 10 in the country in turnover-worthy play rate (6%). Mateer is the biggest reason why OU has the lowest offensive success rate in the SEC (39.2%) and is 109th in the country in PPG (22.0). This year's Texas defense is even better, too, sitting No. 3 in net adjusted EPA per play, No. 11 in success rate (36.5%), and No. 16 in havoc rate (20.6%). Texas has the talent to hand Oklahoma its fourth double-digit Red River Rivalry loss of the Venables era. Score prediction: Texas 24, Oklahoma 13 Who are the stars of Texas vs Oklahoma 2026? Arch Manning, QB, Texas Though Arch Manning hasn't played up to his preseason Heisman Trophy odds , he is one of the most talented quarterbacks in the country. The former No. 1 recruit is a few weeks removed from leading an improbable comeback against Ohio State and ranks 11th in the Power Four in big-time throw rate (5.9%). Last year against a top-notch Sooners defense, Manning finished with an 89.5 QBR and a 91.3% adjusted completion percentage. If he can be that efficient against OU again this year, Texas should cruise to a win, and Manning will reignite the chatter around him as the potential No. 1 pick this April. Isaiah Sategna III, WR, Oklahoma There isn't much to get excited about with this Oklahoma offense, but Isaiah Sategna III is a future NFL player and by far the Sooners' scariest playmaker. In his first season with the program last year after transferring from Arkansas, Sategna led the Sooners in yards from scrimmage by a large margin (989) and was third in the SEC in YAC (524). He's been the lone bright spot again this year, leading the team in scrimmage yards (284) while being one of the country's best punt returners. For OU to pull off the upset, it needs its superstar slot receiver to torch Texas. Trevor Goosby/Melvin Siani, OT, Texas While Manning has been sacked 10 times in four games, that has more to do with his indecisiveness than it does with his offensive line. The Longhorns' signal caller has the 12th-highest time to throw in the country (3.13), and despite that, his star offensive tackles have allowed a combined 11 pressures and two sacks. Coming into the season, Trevor Goosby was viewed as one of the country's best tackles and a potential first-round pick, but Melvin Siani flew under the radar. Siani, a Wake Forest transfer, has been as good as Goosby and is playing himself into the first-round conversation. The Sooners are 12th in the country in havoc rate (21.6%), so Texas needs Goosby and Siani to keep Manning clean to win. David Stone/Taylor Wein, DL, Oklahoma Oklahoma's most talented player is David Stone, and its most disruptive is Taylor Wein. Stone came into the season as a potential first-round pick and Wein as a potential top-100 pick. While Stone hasn't had the impact that was expected of him (just three pressures, two TFLs, 0.5 sack), he's the Sooners' X-factor with his twitch and active hands. At his best, the former five-star recruit is one of the most disruptive interior defensive linemen in the country. Wein, meanwhile, has been OU's best defender (14 defensive stops, 4.5 TFLs). The defensive line duo will need to create havoc against Texas and pressure Manning if Oklahoma's going to have any shot at an upset. Last year in Red River, Stone and Wein combined for five pressures and four TFLs. Colin Simmons, EDGE, Texas There's an argument that Colin Simmons has been the best defensive player in college football through the first few weeks. The projected top-five pick has been borderline unblockable, and in Texas' last game against Tennessee, he set the single-game school record for sacks (5.5). Simmons is top 10 in the Power Four in pressures (18) and is second nationally in sacks (7.5). He's as explosive as he is relentless and will be a massive problem for Oklahoma, especially with how turnover-prone Mateer has been this season. Last year, the Sooners couldn't stop his disruption as he tallied 2.5 sacks to win the Longhorns the Golden Hat. Peyton & Eli Bowen, DB, Oklahoma Everyone knows Peyton and Eli Manning, and their burnt orange-wearing nephew, Arch, but there's another pair of brothers named Peyton and Eli with NFL futures suiting up on the other side of the Red River Rivalry. Peyton (Oklahoma's starting safety) and Eli Bowen (Oklahoma's starting cornerback) are both from Texas, but don the crimson and cream of the Sooners. They're also two of the best defensive backs in the SEC and tied for the lead in forced incompletions at Oklahoma this season (three). Neither is allowing an NFL QB rating above 65.0 when targeted either, and they could be a huge thorn in Arch's side. OU needs the Bowen brothers to lock down the back end of its defense in Red River this year. Texas vs Oklahoma rivalry history: Red River Rivalry 8 (1940-1947) Longest win streak 6 (1952-1957) Largest margin of victory 977-401-34 (.704) Program record 962-355-53 (.722) Claimed national titles (recognized) Conference championships Heisman winners Consensus All-Americans Weeks in the AP Poll Weeks at No. 1 Bowl games (record) NFL draft picks First-round picks This is one of college football's most competitive rivalries because both Texas and Oklahoma have had national success . It also adds to the lore that Texas has been the more successful team in the Red River Rivalry, while Oklahoma has had more national success over the last few decades. Like a river, the rivalry has ebbed and flowed for decades, with Hall of Fame coaches taking over, ending losing streaks, and winning national championships. Red River is one of the defining rivalries in all of sports. The rivalry began in 1900 with a 28-2 win for Texas , and the Longhorns wouldn't lose to Oklahoma until the eighth meeting in 1905, when the Sooners won 2-0. Texas dominated the rivalry ini

picks.blurb: Early odds have Texas and Oklahoma in a total slugfest, with Horns coming out on top Skip to main content Recruiting Women's sports Men's Basketball Women's basketball Softball and Baseball Texas Longhorns history FanSided NCAA Sites Finally, and I mean finally, it is time to see if the Texas Longhorns can hold the Oklahoma Sooners touchdown-less for a third season in a row. As of today, it has been 1,094 days since OU reached the end zone, dating back to the Sooners' 2023 upset (fluke) win over the Horns. However, even as Texas has held Oklahoma to just three field goals over the last two Red River Rivalries, the Longhorns haven't exactly put on offensive showcases . This year, the expectations for the offenses aren't all that different, and the oddsmakers have the 2026 Red River Rivalry as low-scoring as the last couple of seasons. But don't worry, they still have the Horns coming out on top. Early odds for No. 1 Texas vs. Oklahoma in Red River Rivalry Spread: -7.5 Texas, +7.5 Oklahoma Moneyline: -330 Texas, +260 Oklahoma Over/Under: +/-39.5 points While the oddsmakers have Texas walking away with a victory by more than a touchdown, they also have the point total set below 40 points between the two teams. In other words, they expect the final score to be somewhere around 23-16 or 24-16, seemingly alluding to the idea that the Sooners will be able to find the end zone in the Cotton Bowl, a first in nearly 1,100 days by the time the game kicks off on Saturday. The moneyline favors Texas a little more heavily, with someone having to bet $330 on the Horns just to profit $100, but only having to wager $100 on Oklahoma to walk away with a $260 profit. If you ask me, 16 points is way too high a score for an OU offense that has looked even worse than it did over the last two years, especially when you consider how dominant the Texas defense was through the first four games. The Horns have allowed just 13.3 points per game so far this season, and that includes matchups against the then-No. 1 Ohio State Buckeyes and then-No. 14 Tennessee Volunteers. Meanwhile, in Oklahoma's only Power Conference games (losses to the then-unranked Michigan Wolverines and No. 2 Georgia Bulldogs), the Sooners have only averaged 11.5 points per game, and most of that is coming from the defense or special teams. Also read: 3 weaknesses in Oklahoma's game that Texas must exploit in Red River Rivalry On the other side of the ball, Texas's point total almost entirely relies on 1) the offensive line's ability to maintain protection and 2) quarterback Arch Manning's ability to make the right decisions. Yes, the Horns obviously need to get the run game going again, but Manning's level of play seems to determine how well Texas performs on offense. Texas and Oklahoma are scheduled to kick off at 2:30 p.m. CT on Saturday, Oct. 10, and the game will be broadcast on ABC. It's time to see which dominant defense is better and which offense can finally answer the call. Loading recommendations... picks.headline: No. 1 Texas vs. Oklahoma preview: Reeling Sooners look to pull off upset
picks.blurb: No. 1 Texas vs. Oklahoma preview: Reeling Sooners look to pull off upset | Burnt Orange Nation Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Texas Longhorns Community Burnt Orange Nation October 7, 2026 Burnt Orange Nation Notifications Notifications Get The App Sections Texas Longhorns Recruiting Betting FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Texas Football Odds Texas Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Community Guidelines Login / Sign Up Search Get The App Sections Expand Texas Longhorns Recruiting Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds All communities Notifications Texas Longhorns Football The Sooners head to Dallas with a struggling offense and stingy defense. Fresh off a bye week with a 4-0 record, the No. 1 Texas Longhorns head up I-35 for the annual Red River Rivalry against the Oklahoma Sooners, who have struggled thus far in 2026 — Oklahoma has a 2-2 record on the year and has failed to score more than 14 points in each of their last three contests. On paper, this is a matchup that should favor the Longhorns, but if history has shown anything, nothing matters once these two teams take the field at the Cotton Bowl. Scoring points against the Oklahoma defense is doable but will undoubtedly be the biggest challenge facing the Longhorns. “This is always a unique game because you can take record, stats, and all those things and throw them out the window,” Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian said on Monday. “You’ve got to play the game and you’ve got to play the game the right way.” The struggles for the Sooners start on the offensive end. Returning quarterback John Mateer has failed to effectively move the ball through the air and the running attack ranks 131st in the FBS in yards per game. Second-year offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle has made his money with Mateer at the helm, a partnership that is now in it’s fourth year and dates back to their time together at Washington State, but is currently testing the patience of Oklahoma fans given the offense’s lack of scoring. “Coach Venables, I know he’s probably sitting there thinking he wishes the record was a little bit different, but man, his teams play hard, and this team’s no different,” Sarkisian said. “They play hard. They’re an excellent defensive football team. They’ve got draft picks all over on the defense. Offensively, they’ve got playmaking ability similar to us. They’re trying to find their way to to find that level of consistency. But one thing I can be assured of — we’re going to get their best shot, and so I think it’s important for us that we focus on what we need to do so that we can play our best football.” With concerns across the Sooner offense, this year’s rendition will likely be determined by the success of the Longhorns finding the end zone in the Cotton Bowl. If the Longhorns can score points, things could get out of hand. Here’s what to expect on Saturday. As mentioned, the Oklahoma offense is headed by Arbuckle and Mateer. Arbuckle is a young and forward-thinking coordinator with a track record of quarterback development and roots in the Air Raid. At 31 years old, he has already helped develop Bailey Zappe, Austin Reed, and Cam Ward. His offense utilizes tempo and the run game to stretch defenses and create passing windows. With the athleticism of Mateer and the inability to create an impactful rushing attack otherwise, Arbuckle has adapted the offense to feature a quarterback run threat on nearly every play. Averaging just 22 points per game and coming off a bye week, a few new wrinkles are all but guaranteed from Arbuckle on Saturday. Much has been made of Mateer’s play at quarterback this season. The returning starter for the Sooners came into the season with lofty expectations after a turnover-prone 2025 season. Through four games, his play has been disappointing, prompting Venables to admit that he considered benching his starting quarterback at halftime of the Georgia loss. Mateer has completed 66.1 percent of his passes for 883 yards and eight touchdowns while adding 41 carries for 76 yards. However, Mateer has turned the ball over six times in four games, including three first-half turnovers last week against Georgia. Pro Football Focus has tracked eight throws by Mateer as turnover worthy this season. Holding on to the ball is priority number one for Mateer, who has looked rattled in the pocket the season. He’s missed reads, held on to the ball, and fired inaccurately on numerous occasions. Keeping Mateer uncomfortable sets the tone for the Texas defense. Nearly everything else is downstream of whether the Longhorn front can keep him guessing and rushed. Keeping Mateer’s legs out of the game will be another key for Texas — if Mateer can extend plays or effectively pick up first downs on designed runs, things get significantly more complicated for the Longhorn defense. Expect a heavy dose of quick, high-completion throws to start the game in order to neutralize the Texas pass rush and get Mateer into a rhythm. The lead back for the Sooners is junior Lloyd Avant. Avant is a 5’10, 212-pound ball carrier from Humble who has racked up 164 yards and a touchdown on 42 carries (3.9 YPC). A transfer from Colorado State, Avant was expected to compete for snaps with Tory Blaylock, but has been thrust into the starting role due to Blaylock’s hamstring injury. Against UTEP, Avant looked strong, rushing for 79 yards on 15 carries; however, in the three games since, he has carried the ball 27 times for just 85 yards. Blaylock came into the season as the leading back, but is recovering from injury. He’s gotten a handful of carries, but its clear that the coaching staff does have not believe he is close to 100 percent. With an additional week to recover, it’s very possible that he contributes in a more meaningful way on Saturday. Regardless of who takes handoffs, improvement is needed on the ground. After finishing 113th in rushing offense last season, the Sooners are 133rd in yards per rush and t-134th with two rushing touchdowns on the season. Despite an offseason of revamping the rushing attack, things have regressed through four games. “It’s frustrating because I feel like I’m not doing my part,” said tight end Rocky Beers , via OU Insider . “There’s always one miss here, one miss there, and it’s costing us... We’ve just got to believe in our blocks and hold onto them as long as we can.” Getting back to running the ball was undoubtedly a point of emphasis over the bye week and something that the Longhorns will need to thwart on Saturday. Wide receiver Perhaps the most talented player on the Sooner offense is leading wide receiver Isaiah Sategna. A transfer from Arkansas, Sategna leads the offense in receptions (20), yards (267), and longest play from scrimmage (53). His two touchdowns are tied for the most on the team. Listed at 5’10, Sategna isn’t a huge target but can be dangerous. His quickness can generate missed tackles and additional yardage after the catch, so closing in quickly will be important come Saturday. Sategna forced 22 missed tackles last season and half of his receiving yards this season have come after the catch. Transfers Trell Harris and Parker Livingstone were brought in to supplement Sategna but neither has been effective thus far. Harris remains sidelined with an injury and Livingstone hasn’t been able to make a difference, though this will undoubtedly be a big game for him after transferring from Texas during the offseason. Stopping Sategna will be the key to keeping the wide outs locked down, a task that Longhorns defensive coordinator Will Muschamp has to feel good about. Veteran tight end Rocky Beers, a Colorado State transfer, has proved to be a reliable weapon for Mateer in the passing game, tallying 18 catches for 255 yards and two touchdowns this season, which is the best on the team outside of Sategna. One of three tight ends brought in from the portal by new position coach Jason Witten, Beers has looked the part this season. His route running creates windows for Mateer and he has enough size to be a matchup problem on smaller defenders. When Oklahoma makes it to the red zone, Beers is a frequent target, something that Texas will need to take away come Saturday. Offensive line The running game has struggled for the Sooners and a big reason for that falls on the shoulders of the offensive line. This group has failed to keep a clean pocket, generate push, and open running lanes. If Oklahoma hopes to turn things around offensively, the five up front will need to step up their performance, immediately. Against Georgia, the Oklahoma offensive line switched things up, sitting Eddy Pierre-Louis at guard in favor of Heath Ozaeta and Noah Best, but it made little difference. E’Marion Harris, the right tackle, still looked a step slow while star left tackle Michael Fasusi remains sidelined with a shoulder injury. I’d expect this group to get additional help in blocking from tight ends and running backs, as well as a heavy dose of plays designed to get the ball out of Mateer’s hand quickly. This group has yet to show anything special through four games, increasing pressure on longtime position coach Bill Bedenbaugh, whose tenure dates to the Bob Stoops era. The Oklahoma offense has sputtered to start the year. Poor quarterback play coupled with a lack of rushing attack and porous offensive line has resulted in little points being scored. With a bye week to prepare for the Longhorns, I’d expect a sharpened game plan out of the gate that features quick passes and unique ways to get the ball out of Mateer’s hands. For the Longhorn defense to find success, getting pressure is key. When Mateer feels the pass rush, he has shown an inability to make good reads and deliver accurate passes. Keeping him from feeling comfortable will be a point of emphasis for the Longhorns. Outside of Mateer, limiting Sategna and Beers is the next priority. Forcing someone besides these three players to make a difference should spell success for the Longhorns. For every concern about the offense, the defense boasts a strength. This unit has been salty thanks to a solid crop of returners despite a mediocre offense on the other side of the ball that can’t finish drives and turns the ball over. Moving the ball through the air against the Sooners has been particularly tough. Allowing 122.5 passing yards per game, the OU secondary ranks fourth in the country, and is led by returning producers that understand the scheme and have the physical talent to implement it successfully. Opponents convert 23.1 percent of third downs, the third best in the entire country, meaning staying ahead of the chains will be essential for the Texas offense. The best method to attack this defense has been via the run. Averaging 115.5 yards per game on the ground and 3.23 yards per carry, this aspect remains in the top third of the country but lags behind the stellar pass and third-down defense. Don’t be mistaken by the record or score against Georgia — the Oklahoma defense can get after it. Defensive line Up front, there are four players that Texas will need to handle — defensive ends Taylor Wein and Adepoju Adebawore, and tackles David Stone and Jayden Jackson. In the middle, Stone and Jackson are a formidable duo. Stone was one of the Sooners’ most highly-regarded returners after notching 43 tackles a year ago. Now in his third year at Oklahoma, the 6’3, 312-pound lineman will be looking for his first win in Dallas. Next to him, Jackson is quite the player. Last season, he tallied 28 tackles and 3.0 sacks, including being honored as the Outland Trophy National Player of the Week for his performance against Auburn. This duo up front has been a big reason why the defense has been stout thus far. away.headline: Steve Sarkisian breaks down how Texas football can beat Oklahoma in Red River Rivalry
away.blurb: “The team that runs the ball, the team that converts their downs, the team that wins a turnover battle, and the team that can pressure the quarterback generally comes out on top. It generally comes back to the things that are important to football, right?” Sarkisian said. The college football Week 6 schedule will feature a highly anticipated game between Texas football and the Oklahoma Sooners. The Red River Rivalry returns to the Cotton Bowl, and Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian already has a clear idea of what his team needs to do to get past the Sooners. During his Tuesday press conference, Sarkisian explained that the game could ultimately come down to which team executes the fundamental aspects of football better and continued by breaking down his plan . Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) In the head coach’s view, Texas must be able to consistently move the chains while also forcing Oklahoma into mistakes and making life difficult for its quarterback. While Texas enters the rivalry as the higher-ranked team, Sarkisian is not overlooking Oklahoma. He added that Sooners head coach Brent Venables may wish his team’s record looked different. But he expects Oklahoma to play with the same intensity and physicality it has shown throughout the season. “They’re an excellent defensive football team. They’ve got draft picks all over on the defense. Offensively, they’ve got play-making ability. Similar to us, they’re trying to find their way to find that level of consistency, but one thing I can be sure of, we’re going to get their best shot.” Texas is ranked No. 1 and enters the packed Week 6 schedule undefeated at 4-0. Meanwhile, Oklahoma sits at 2-2 and will be looking to pull off a major upset against the top-ranked Longhorns. On paper, the upcoming game appears to favor Texas. Moreover, the Longhorns enter the game with some recent momentum in the rivalry after defeating Oklahoma 23-6 in the 2025 meeting. Still, the history of the Red River Rivalry has repeatedly shown that records and rankings can quickly become secondary once Texas and Oklahoma meet in Dallas. Like ClutchPoints’ content? away.blurb: Well, this week's message is along that exact same vein, with the Horns' head coach denying to provide any additional context ahead of releasing the first availability report of the week, which comes out at 7:10 p.m. CT on Wednesday evening. Both were listed as "OUT" on the final availability report for Week 4 , alongside defensive back Xavier Filsaime and offensive lineman Jordan Coleman. For now, one could hope (and reasonably assume, based on Sarkisian's message about getting healthier) that at least one of those players is ready for, or close to ready for, action in the rivalry game. Texas gives injury non-update on Hollywood Smothers, Nick Townsend status once again Skip to main content Recruiting After nearly a week and a half since we last saw the Texas Longhorns take the field against the Tennessee Volunteers, many people were eager to hear how previously injured players had progressed over the bye. However, what should come as no surprise is that Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian had another idea in mind : no update. With star players like running back Hollywood Smothers, tight end Nick Townsend, and defensive lineman Justus Terry all missing time this season, Longhorn Nation has been eager to see their guys back in action. Unfortunately, we will have to wait to see what we should expect on Saturday. "I think we're healthier than we were a week ago at this time," Sarkisian said in his game preview press conference, continuing his refusal to share injury updates beyond what he puts in the SEC-mandated availability reports. Steve Sarkisian sticks to SEC availability report and nothing more On Monday of Week 4, before the Horns faced the Vols, Sarkisian expressed a similar sentiment, refusing to update members of the media on any lingering injuries, stating that "There's called an injury report in the SEC, so that's enough of the injury questions," Sarkisian said that week. Based on the final injury list from Texas's game against Tennessee, one could easily assume that Smothers will be good to go against the Oklahoma Sooners this weekend as the Horns prepare for the annual Red River Rivalry. The star running back was off the report just before kickoff and was seen on the sidelines in full pads, with his helmet on, but never entered the game against the Volunteers. However, when it comes to Terry and Townsend, your guess is as good as mine. Smothers is nursing a reported lower-leg injury suffered in practice, Townsend is healing up from a knee injury he sustained before Week 2's kickoff, Terry is recovering from a toe injury ahead of Week 2's game, Coleman hasn't played since Week 3, and Filsaime has yet to take the field this season. For right now, Texas fans (and Oklahoma fans) will have to wait to see what Texas's injury list looks like on Wednesday evening, because until then, Sarkisian is remaining tight-lipped about the health of his team. "Mikey's a big piece of the team, and we're gonna be with him while he's recovering that foot, and we'll get him back, and that'll make us an even better team," Ogden said. home.blurb: “The team that runs the ball, the team that converts their downs, the team that wins a turnover battle, and the team that can pressure the quarterback generally comes out on top. The college football Week 6 schedule will feature a highly anticipated game between Texas football and the Oklahoma Sooners. The Red River Rivalry returns to the Cotton Bowl, and Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian already has a clear idea of what his team needs to do to get past the Sooners. But he expects Oklahoma to play with the same intensity and physicality it has shown throughout the season. “They’re an excellent defensive football team. They’ve got draft picks all over on the defense. Offensively, they’ve got play-making ability. Similar to us, they’re trying to find their way to find that level of consistency, but one thing I can be sure of, we’re going to get their best shot.” Texas is ranked No. 1 and enters the packed Week 6 schedule undefeated at 4-0. Meanwhile, Oklahoma sits at 2-2 and will be looking to pull off a major upset against the top-ranked Longhorns. On paper, the upcoming game appears to favor Texas. Moreover, the Longhorns enter the game with some recent momentum in the rivalry after defeating Oklahoma 23-6 in the 2025 meeting. The biggest positive involves running back Hollywood Smothers, who missed the Tennessee game despite dressing in an emergency role. The following bye week gave Texas additional time to get its leading rusher healthy. That could matter considerably against Oklahoma. Smothers leads Texas with 198 rushing yards on 41 carries and gives the Longhorns another physical option alongside Raleek Brown and Derrek Cooper. Texas managed without him at Tennessee, but getting Smothers back would make life considerably easier for quarterback Arch Manning. Wide receiver Cam Coleman also appears to be trending toward full availability after suffering a bruised tailbone against Tennessee. Coleman returned to that game, and Sarkisian described the injury as nothing serious. His presence opposite Ryan Wingo is important because Texas needs its vertical passing game intact against an Oklahoma defense likely to challenge Manning with pressure and disguised coverages. The bigger uncertainty may be on defense. Terry’s status could be particularly important. Oklahoma’s offense will test Texas between the tackles, and having another disruptive interior lineman would allow the Longhorns to keep their defensive front fresh while freeing star edge rusher Colin Simmons to attack the quarterback. picks.headline: Early preview of No. 23 UCLA Bruins ahead of Oregon Ducks showdown
picks.blurb: Early preview of No. 23 UCLA Bruins ahead of Oregon Ducks showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Yamamoto, Dodgers beat Braves Messi's Argentina farewell Padres avoid NLDS sweep NFL Power Rankings Gauff decries racist posts Early preview of No. 23 UCLA Bruins ahead of Oregon Ducks showdown Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Oregon Ducks are in the midst of a much-needed bye week, enjoying some time off after a strenuous and pressure-filled first month of the 2026 season. Through four games, we've seen the Ducks start at No. 2 in the AP poll, drop to No. 6 after an underwhelming win over Boise State before losing to Oklahoma State, dropping them all the way down to No. 21. They then took care of Portland State, 84-0, moving them up a spot before a pivotal road matchup in Los Angeles with USC . The Ducks never blinked, even when quarterback Dante Moore had to leave the game via ambulance with a head injury, as backup Dylan Raiola and some timely defensive plays powered Oregon over USC, 41-27. It was as impressive of a win as we've seen from the Ducks over the past two seasons, and one that they badly needed in order to keep their goals of winning a national championship alive. Now, Oregon gets to take a breath and relax with a Week 5 bye. But that's not all that the players and staff are doing, as they'll be getting a jumpstart on preparing for the upstart UCLA Bruins , who will come to town in Week 6. We'll follow suit, providing an early deep-dive preview of how the Bruins ' season has gone so far, a breakdown of the offense, defense, special teams and players to watch with game and betting details to boot. Let's start with UCLA's resume, as they head into the matchup with Oregon looking to continue their undefeated season. UCLA's Resume Through Five Weeks Sep 26, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; UCLA Bruins wide receiver Aidan Mizell (1) dances in the end zone with wide receiver Landon Ellis (11) and wide receiver Semaj Morgan (4) after catching an 83-yard touchdown reception in the second half against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images Week 1: W 45-24 @ Cal Week 2: W 28-10 vs. San Diego State Week 3: W 52-38 vs. Purdue Week 4: W 52-3 @ Maryland The Bruins got off to an impressive start in the newly-hired Bob Chesney era, taking down the Tosh Lupoi-led Golden Bears on the road after a dominant second half. Chesney, who commanded James Madison to the College Football Playoff a year ago, relied upon several of his former Dukes that followed him to Westwood in the season-opener. The start of the season was strong, and so was last game for UCLA. The Bruins went into Maryland and stomped all over the Terrapins, picking off four passes and racking up 475 total yards. The early, 10:30 PT start didn't hold them back, as they jumped out to a 20-3 lead at halftime and only added to the lead after the break. Sandwiched between those two spectacular outings were victories over San Diego State and Purdue, with the offense carrying them in the former and offense in the latter, showing how well-rounded the Bruins are in 2026. Offensive Breakdown Sep 26, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; UCLA Bruins running back Jaivian Thomas (21) celebrates with offensive line Hall Schmidt (65) after scoring a touchdown in the first half against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images While last season was discombobulated at times for the Bruins offensively, new coordinator Dean Kennedy — coming over with Chesney from James Madison — has brought a revitalized, intelligent and, thus far, highly-successful offense to UCLA. Kennedy has a history of elevating previously subpar offensive units, as he developed quarterback Kyle Trask at Florida, turned Holy Cross into the Patriot League scoring leader and orchestrated the ninth-ranked scoring offense at James Madison in 2025. Now, he's doing the same thing at UCLA with a spread-based system that emphasizes physicality and explosiveness at the point of attack. Kennedy's units have consistently been among the best at creating explosive plays, both on the ground and through the air. While the Bruins won't go under center much at all, instead standing in the shotgun or pistol, they aren't afraid to run it right down the defense's throat. Through the air, the route combinations aren't necessarily complex, but they make it easy on the quarterback to read with a progression-based system. Defensive Breakdown Sep 26, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; UCLA Bruins linebacker Trent Hendrick (25) celebrates after intercepting a pass in the second half against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images Also brought over from James Madison, Colin Hitschler is the defensive coordinator for the Bruins with a goal of instilling an uncommon physicality that hasn't been seen in Westwood for some time. And thus far this fall, UCLA has, for the most part, lived up those goals. The Bruins mostly operate out of a 4-2-5 defensive alignment, following the trend of opting to put an extra defensive back on the field over a lumbering linebacker. But make no mistake, the linebackers have plenty of talent to handle the middle of the field themselves, with a pair of seniors coming in at first and second on the team in tackles through four games. Hitschler isn't afraid to send pressure, having loads of success against Maryland in forcing the quarterback to make decisions under duress that turned into four interceptions. Expect more of the same come Week 6, with Hitschler putting the onus on the offensive line to protect whoever trots out at quarterback for the Ducks. Special Teams Breakdown Sep 12, 2026; Pasadena, California, USA; UCLA kicker Mateen Bhaghani (15) kicks a field-goal during the second half against San Diego State at the Rose Bowl. Mandatory Credit: William Liang-Imagn Images The Bruins have modest special teams units, with average kickoff and punt return marks with the same for the coverage units — though the return aspect could change in a blink with a pair of return men with elite speed waiting back there. In the kicking game, kicker Mateen Bhaghani has been solid in converting 4-of-5 field goals and all 23 extra points. It's his third season as the starter at UCLA, and he's made 82.8% of his field goals with a long of 57 yards — a massive advantage at the college level. Punter Curtis Gerrand also has a big leg, averaging 45.7 yards per punt on 15 boots thus far. Players to Watch Sep 26, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; UCLA Bruins quarterback Nico Iamaleava (9) passes in the first half against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images There's an abundance of talent across the roster, yet these three players will have to be accounted for by the Ducks if they're to get their fourth win. QB Nico Iamaleava 2026 Season Stats: 62-for-99, 820 yards, 4 TDs, 2 INTs / / 35 rushes, 143 yards, 1 TD Analysis: Iamaleava hasn't quite needed to show off his world-class athleticism this year, with his backfield mate stealing much of the thunder in the first month of the season. That's not to say the former Tennessee starter can't scoot, as he's run for 1,077 yards and 11 touchdowns in four seasons while tossing 38 touchdowns and 14 interceptions. Not the most refined passer, Iamaleava — like many college quarterbacks — feasts on short and long throws, but hasn't quite developed the intermediate aspect of his game. Still very talented, Iamaleava is commanding mid-to-late round draft buzz, though he does have one more season of eligibility remaining. RB Wayne Knight 2026 Season Stats: 49 rushes, 445 yards, 9 TDs / / 8 catches, 88 yards Analysis: Yes, you read that right. Wayne has nine touchdowns four games into the year, with six coming in the first two games. Standing just 5-foot-7 and 193 pounds, Knight makes up for his lack of size with elite speed, vision and playmaking ability. At James Madison in 2025, Knight broke off runs of 73, 59, 58 and 49 yards with 57 and 49-yard gains on receptions. Always an ability to hit a home-run, the Ducks will have to be cognizant not to lose Knight behind the Bruins' offensive line. LB Sammy Omosigho 2026 Season Stats: 37 tackles, 3 sacks, 4 forced fumbles Analysis: Though the Bruins added 2025 Sun Belt Defensive Player of the Year Trent Hendricks to the roster recently, he's still getting acclimated so we'll spotlight Sammy Omosigho here. The 6-foot-2, 239-pound four-year Oklahoma transfer has gotten off to a fast start at UCLA, leading the team in tackles and recording three sacks from his linebacker spot. Hitschler sends the former Sooner quite often on pressures and he makes plays as evidenced by his four forced fumbles in four games. picks.headline: Oregon football comes off bye with game against UCLA. A sneak preview
picks.blurb: When former Dukes coach Bob Chesney made the move to Los Angeles in December, he brought 11 players and almost his entire coaching staff with him. Several of those players are now starting for the No. 22 Bruins (4-0, 2-0 Big Ten), who will be at Autzen Stadium Oct. 10 for a 12:30 p.m. conference game against No. 13 Oregon (3-1, 1-0). "JMUCLA," is how UCLA tight end and James Madison transfer Josh Phifer described his new team earlier this season. Chesney has his new team rolling. Like the Ducks , the Bruins are coming off a bye week . In their last game, they defeated Maryland 54-3 on Sept. 26 and held the Terrapins to 181 yards and one first-half field goal. Chesney's last game at James Madison came at Autzen Stadium on Dec. 20 when Oregon won 51-34 in a College Football Playoff first-round game. Eight starters for JMU in that game are now at UCLA. Here's an early look at the Bruins. Who is UCLA's QB? Nico Iamaleava is thriving in his second season as the Bruins' starter. The 6-5, 215-pound senior, who was the nation's No. 1 overall recruit in 2023, has thrown for 820 yards and four touchdowns, and has rushed for 143 and one TD. Last year he was one-man show at UCLA when he threw for 1,928 yards and 13 touchdowns with seven interceptions while also leading the Bruins in rushing yards (505), carries (112) and rushing touchdowns (4). Other UCLA offensive standouts Running back Wayne Knight is second in the Big Ten with 445 rushing yards and leads the conference with nine rushing touchdowns. The former James Madison star is averaging 9.1 yards per carry and 111.3 per game. The 5-7, 193-pound fifth year was a second-team All-American in 2025 after totaling 2,039 all-purpose yards. Michigan transfer Semaj Morgan is the Bruins' top receiver with 14 receptions for 174 yards and two touchdowns – all team highs. Defensive standouts for UCLA Senior linebacker Sammy Omosigho has been terrorizing opposing offenses this season. The transfer from Oklahoma leads the Bruins with 40 tackles (27 solo), 7.5 tackles for loss, three sacks and four forced fumbles. Safety Ta'Shawn James, a transfer from Iowa State, has 24 tackles and a conference-leading three interceptions, including a pick-six against Maryland. Former Oregon reserve Rodrick Pleasant is in his second season starting at cornerback for UCLA. He was all-Big Ten honorable mention in 2025. The last time the Ducks and Bruins met Oregon defeated UCLA 34-13 at the Rose Bowl on Sept. 28, 2024, in what was the Ducks' first conference game as a member of the Big Ten. "Similar to what we said before, we're gonna do what's best for Dante moving forward," Lanning said. "It was great to see him back out there with his teammates getting to work today." The Big Ten's injury report comes out Wednesday evening, with daily updates mandated through two hours prior to Saturday's kickoff. Mid-week designations include probable, questionable, doubtful or out. The team physician determines "pre-participation clearance and/or the need for additional consultation or testing." The NCAA mandates that when an athlete shows signs of a concussion, they are not allowed to return to the game. The NCAA's concussion safety protocol management guidelines state that a player's return to play is a step-by-step process that must be completed without symptoms returning -- almost like weather delays, when a single streak of lightning in the area delays a return to action. The five stages of an athlete's return to play via the NCAA are as follows: Stage 1: Symptom-limited activity: Begin with light aerobic exercise. Stage 5: Return to competition: An athlete can return to game play only after successfully completing all prior stages and receiving medical clearance. With Monday's return to practice, the next update from Lanning and the Ducks' coaching staff on Moore comes later this week. Given Moore's status and Raiola's play off the bench, Lanning has a difficult choice on who to play in the coming weeks if his starter is ready to return to action. Raiola completed 19 of 25 passes for 289 yards and two touchdowns against USC, executing Oregon's offense to near perfection in the second half of the win over the Trojans. This comes after the Ducks had looked out of rhythm several times in the early going this fall, following a near-stumble against Boise State and a loss at Oklahoma State.
