"Similar to what we said before, we're gonna do what's best for Dante moving forward," Lanning said. "It was great to see him back out there with his teammates getting to work today." The Big Ten's injury report comes out Wednesday evening, with daily updates mandated through two hours prior to Saturday's kickoff. Mid-week designations include probable, questionable, doubtful or out. The team physician determines "pre-participation clearance and/or the need for additional consultation or testing." The NCAA mandates that when an athlete shows signs of a concussion, they are not allowed to return to the game. The NCAA's concussion safety protocol management guidelines state that a player's return to play is a step-by-step process that must be completed without symptoms returning -- almost like weather delays, when a single streak of lightning in the area delays a return to action. The five stages of an athlete's return to play via the NCAA are as follows: Stage 1: Symptom-limited activity: Begin with light aerobic exercise. Stage 5: Return to competition: An athlete can return to game play only after successfully completing all prior stages and receiving medical clearance. With Monday's return to practice, the next update from Lanning and the Ducks' coaching staff on Moore comes later this week. Given Moore's status and Raiola's play off the bench, Lanning has a difficult choice on who to play in the coming weeks if his starter is ready to return to action. Raiola completed 19 of 25 passes for 289 yards and two touchdowns against USC, executing Oregon's offense to near perfection in the second half of the win over the Trojans. This comes after the Ducks had looked out of rhythm several times in the early going this fall, following a near-stumble against Boise State and a loss at Oklahoma State. home.headline: Oregon Ducks players excited to see QB Dante Moore practicing, believe in Dylan Raiola
home.blurb: EUGENE — Oregon Ducks quarterback Dante Moore ’s return to practice, after suffering a concussion and being carted off the field in the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26, was met with enthusiasm from his teammates. “That dude, he out there working already,” defensive tackle A’Mauri Washington said on Tuesday, flashing a big grin. “I tried to get a sack on him earlier.” Protecting Moore could require holding him out of the team’s upcoming game. No. 13 Oregon (3-1, 1-0 Big Ten) will host No. 21 UCLA (4-0, 2-0) at 12:30 p.m. Saturday. Moore must complete several steps to be cleared for game action. His return to practice indicates positive progress in his recovery. “He’s out there having fun again with a smile on his face,” Iuli said. “It’s been impressive,” linebacker Jerry Mixon said. “He’s been ready. He hasn’t laid back since he was a backup quarterback. He’s been ready the whole time, learning from Dante. He’s been starting for two years. So he knows what to do when he gets out there.” YouTube's privacy policy is available here and YouTube's terms of service is available here . On Monday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning said that the plan is to do what’s best for Moore’s health and that an injury report would be released later this week. Raiola, who started two seasons at Nebraska before transferring, passed for 289 yards and two touchdowns against the Trojans (5-1, 2-1) after replacing Moore in the second quarter. home.headline: Oregon's Dave Iuli Gets Candid on Mentoring Ducks' Young Offensive Linemen
home.blurb: Dave Iuli is one of two players who returned after starting every game on the offensive line for the Ducks in 2025. With a rotation of linemen – which heavily consists of freshmen and sophomores – switching in and out, Iuli’s role as a leader becomes more critical. “So being a mentor has not only helped the youngins, but it’s helped me as well for if I ever want to be a future coach or just coaching somebody else up,” Iuli said. “I feel like it helps them as well because they know when we get out of here, now we need them to be mentors, and it carries on the legacy here." One specific player who Iuli’s developed a bond with is the interior lineman, Keli. The true freshman was a three-star recruit coming out of Honolulu, Hawaii, but is someone who could be vying for a potential starting center role later down the line. “So, I think having him out there and being a guy that can lead block for us and being a young guy that we could just be reliable on has been really good so far for Koloi,” he added. “He keeps that up, he’s gonna do great in the future.” The massive shakeup in personnel along the offensive line was one of the key storylines during fall camp and entering the No. 13 Oregon Ducks’ season. While an upset loss to Oklahoma State and an injury scare for quarterback Dante Moore against the USC Trojans have been among the key concerns for Ducks fans, questions about the offensive line linger. Mentoring Oregon’s Next Batch of Offensive Linemen Outside of center offensive lineman Iapani “Poncho” Laloulu, there hasn’t been much consistency for the unit both between seasons and at the start of 2026. A season-ending injury to left guard Trent Ferguson caused more shifting along the line , while true freshmen Immanuel Iheanacho, Tommy Tofi and Koloi Keli’s growth has resulted in more snaps for the freshmen. Add in that players like sophomores Ziyare Addison and Douglas Utu have gained larger roles, and Iuli’s potential as a leading voice in the locker room and on the field is vital. “I’ll say my factor as a mentor has been huge just being an older guy around these young guys because it takes stress off the coaches, too,” Iuli said on Tuesday. “I feel like when every day you got youngins coming in it almost gets repetitive of the same questions they’re asking.” “So, it’s so important for guys like me, Poncho, Kawika (Rogers), all the older guys, to be in there and be in the young guys ear of, letting them know, ‘Hey, this is what we do here. This is how it goes. This is the play. This is what we’re doing,’” he continued. Iuli is a fifth-year for the Ducks, but he came off his 2025 season with a torn tricep. He wasn’t featured as heavily in the season opener against Boise State, but he told the media on Tuesday that he’s “fully back at 100 percent.” His newfound mentorship role not only benefits offensive line coach A’lique Terry and Oregon coach Dan Lanning. home.headline: Oregon QB Dante Moore returns to practice, per Dan Lanning
home.blurb: Quarterback Dante Moore , who suffered a serious concussion in a win against USC, did practice on Monday with the Ducks , according to Lanning. It remains unclear if Moore will play or sit out on Saturday, as Lanning deflected questions around the star quarterback's availability to the Big Ten's mandatory injury reports that will be released throughout the week. "Dante was out there at practice for us today," Lanning told reporters on Monday. "Similar to what we said before, we're going to continue to make sure we do what's best for Dante as we move forward. Obviously, we'll have an injury report that's released later on this week that will detail what that looks like, but it was great to see him back out there with his teammates." "Dylan's got to keep doing what he's been doing," Lanning said. "Preparing like he's going to be the guy that goes out there every single day. We need that from every single person on our team. We don't need anything special from Dylan other than doing what he's been doing." home.headline: Will Stein explains Kentucky’s decision to go for 2-pointer vs. South Carolina, provides injury updates
home.blurb: Kentucky Wildcats head coach Will Stein explained that the Wildcats' limited player availability was a major factor in his decision to go for a two-point conversion in their 35-34 overtime victory over South Carolina on Saturday night. Kentucky entered the game with seven players listed as out, including key contributors wide receiver DJ Miller and linebacker Tavion Wallace. The other unavailable players were linebacker Alex Afari, who became ineligible following a recent court ruling, defensive back Grant Grayton, long snapper Cole Marszalek, offensive lineman Aba Selm, and offensive lineman Jay Clark. With a depleted roster and limited depth, Stein and the Wildcats opted to go for the win rather than kick the extra point and extend the game into a second overtime. Quarterback Kenny Minchey connected with Willie Rodriguez on the successful 2-point conversion to secure the victory. Defensive back Jaden Smith left Saturday's game with an injury that appeared serious. Along with running back Jason Patterson and linebacker Antwan Smith exiting the game, Stein also revealed that defensive back Aaron Gates was a late scratch. Gates had been expected to play but was ultimately not ready to return to the field. "Jaden Smith went out, which was unfortunate towards the end," Stein said. "We're low at star (linebacker). Aaron Gates…we projected him to play. He wasn't able to go today. Kentucky will certainly hope to have key contributors such as Miller and Wallace available as the Wildcats look to build on their thrilling road victory over South Carolina. home.headline: Cal Football Game Summary: Bears Lose to UNLV; Sagapolutele Injured
home.blurb: Cal was without quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele for the entire second half after he left the game in the final minute of the second quarter when he hit his head hard on the turf. He reportedly was cleared to return but Cal opted not put him back in the game with a head injury. Cal safety Kingston Lopa left the game with an injury three minutes into the first quarter and did not return. Bears starting nickel back Cam Sidney was ejected from the game for targeting in the first quarter. Cal defensive back Daniel Harris was ejected for targeting in the fourth quarter. INDIVIDUAL STAT OF THE GAME II: Cal limited all-Mountain West running back Jai'Den "Jet" Thomas to 46 yards on 16 carries. This game was considered a tipping point for Cal’s season, and it tipped the wrong way. Cal’s second straight loss reduces Cal’s chances to finish the season with a winning record for the second straight season. Before the season began, a 4-1 Cal record after five games seemed possible and a 5-0 start was not out of the question. A 2-3 mark at this stage was not what Cal supporters had in mind. The Bears have little momentum heading into the heart of its ACC schedule, which starts next Saturday with a home game against Virginia Tech. The outside complaints from Cal fans will continue, and the Bears are on the verge of becoming irrelevant this season. Cal rallied from a 24-7 halftime deficit to take the lead, but ultimately the Bears lost to UNLV 39-31 on Saturday afternoon at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas. Jackson Brousseau was the Bears' quarterback in the second half. Cal played the game without injured running back Adam Mohammed, the team’s leading rusher with 336 yards. RECORDS: CAL (2-3, 1-1 ACC), UNLV (3-2, 1-0 Mountain West) UNLV quarterback Jackson Arnold. Although he passed for just 158 yards, he threw touchdown passes of 70, 36 and 10 yards and ran for a 55-yard touchdown. He also had a key 42-yard run and finished with 110 rushing yards. With Cal leading 25-24, UNLV quarterback Jackson Arnold ran 42 yards to the Cal 12-yard line, which led to Arnold's 10-yard touchdown pass for a 32-25 UNLV lead with 9:38 left. KEY PLAY 1: On a fourth-and-2 play from the UNLV 47-yard line, Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele completed a pass to Tyree Sams, but it was a half-yard short of a first down. It turned the ball over the UNLV with 12:20 left in the first quarter with the game scoreless. KEY PLAY 2: Cal safety Kingston Lopa, who leads the nation in interceptions with five, left the game with an injury three minutes into the first quarter. KEY PLAY 3: Sagapolutele completed a 91-yard touchdown pass to freshman tight end Taimane Purcell, who covered most of the ground himself. It gave Cal a 7-0 lead with 11:30 remaining in the first quarter. KEY PLAY 4 : Cal starting safety Cam Sidney was ejected for targeting with 11:25 left in the first quarter. KEY PLAY 5: On a third-and-8 play from the UNLV 30-yard line, Rebels quarterback Jackson Arnold completed a 70-yard touchdown

picks.blurb: Georgia @ Alabama Preview And Prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Yamamoto, Dodgers beat Braves Messi's Argentina farewell Padres avoid NLDS sweep NFL Power Rankings Gauff decries racist posts Georgia @ Alabama Preview And Prediction Photo Credit: David Leong Landon Kardian Tue, October 6, 2026 at 3:25 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It does not get much bigger than this. No. 2 Georgia travels to Tuscaloosa Saturday night to face No. 6 Alabama in a 7:30 p.m. kickoff at Bryant-Denny Stadium. Both teams enter 5-0 and 3-0 in SEC play, making this one of the biggest games of the college football season. Georgia absolutely has a path to winning this game. The Bulldogs have the more experienced quarterback in Gunner Stockton, an elite rushing attack and a defense allowing just 13.4 points per game. Stockton has completed 75.5% of his passes with 13 touchdowns and only one interception. But there is one major concern: Can Georgia's defense get enough stops? Keelon Russell has been on fire. He has thrown for 1,414 yards with 11 touchdowns and just two interceptions while adding another four touchdowns on the ground. Alabama just went into Starkville and dropped 56 points on Mississippi State, with Russell throwing for 285 yards and three touchdowns. Georgia's defense has been good statistically, but it hasn't faced anything quite like this Alabama offense. The Bulldogs showed some cracks against Vanderbilt, allowing 293 yards and struggling to consistently get off the field on third down before tightening things up in the second half. Against Russell, those mistakes could become touchdowns. Georgia's best chance is to run the football, control possession and keep Russell standing on the Alabama sideline. Nate Frazier and the Bulldogs' offensive line can absolutely have success, and Stockton's efficiency gives Georgia another way to move the football if Alabama loads the box. The problem is that Alabama can counter by bringing pressure and trusting its secondary. Kirby Smart called Alabama's defensive backs talented, physical "ball hawks" and specifically pointed to the pressure created by the Crimson Tide's front. And then there is Bryant-Denny Stadium . This game being in Tuscaloosa matters. Georgia will be dealing with one of the loudest environments in college football against an Alabama team playing with a ton of confidence. Even the betting market has shifted toward the Crimson Tide, with Alabama currently sitting around a 1.5-point favorite after Georgia initially opened as the favorite. Prediction: Alabama 38, Georgia 27 I trust Georgia to move the football. I trust Stockton's experience, and I think the Bulldogs can establish the run. I just don't trust Georgia to get enough stops. Russell's ability to create outside structure is the difference. Georgia can defend the play perfectly and still watch Russell escape the pocket and turn it into an explosive gain. Add the home-field advantage, Alabama's veteran secondary and the Tide's ability to pressure Stockton, and the matchup starts leaning toward Bama. Georgia hangs around, but eventually Russell makes too many plays. Alabama 38, Georgia 27. Check Out All EasySportz College Football Content Here! College Football Viewing Guide

By Cory Nightingale Published: Oct 4, 2026 · 7:51 PM EDT ESPN's FPI is seeing what most will see this week in the leadup to the massive matchup in Tuscaloosa between No. 2 Georgia and No. 6 Alabama . Saturday night's Week 6 showdown is, naturally, in prime time, with a 7:30 p.m. ET kickoff on ABC, as the SEC superpowers hook up once more with both teams ranked in the top 10 and plenty on the line on the second Saturday of October. By all accounts, this should be a game that comes down to the bitter end in T-Town, and that's what the FPI believes, too. At least for now, Alabama is a very slight favorite at home, and ESPN's FPI follows with that theme by giving the Tide a 52.6% chance to prevail and stay unbeaten. But because Bama is getting just over a 50% chance to win, that means Georgia is getting an almost 50% chance to prevail, too. To be exact, the Dawgs are being given a 47.3% shot to storm into Tuscaloosa and stay unbeaten themselves. Fittingly, both teams have the exact same overall record (5-0) and SEC mark (3-0), so something really does have to give on Saturday night. Not only is this a matchup that features 2 of the best teams in college football in 2026, it's of course a historical SEC showdown that features 2 of the most traditional powers in the conference's history. These 2 behemoths have played for plenty in recent years, and while Alabama leads the all-time series, 45-27-4, Georgia has won plenty over Bama in recent seasons, including beating the Tide in last year's SEC Championship Game as well as outlasting Alabama in the 2021 national championship game. Of course, 4 years earlier, almost to the day, Bama took down Georgia in overtime to win that thriller of a national title game to end the 2017 season. So, it's gone both ways in the biggest of moments, and Saturday night will provide another big moment in a rivalry like none other in the SEC. away.headline: Vanderbilt QB Jared Curtis lands on injury report before Georgia showdown
away.blurb: Curtis landed in the “questionable” category on the injury report released by the SEC Wednesday. This could alter the Commodores’ offense once more under head coach Clark Lea. Vanderbilt football can deliver a massive statement Saturday by stunning No. 2 Georgia. Even after the Bulldogs’ epic beatdown of 2025 College Football Playoff team Oklahoma . But Vandy faces rolling without starting quarterback Jared Curtis for this showdown. Vandy previously turned to an RPO (Run Pass Option) offense with Diego Pavia. Including leaning into Pavia’s mobility to win games. That led to the 5-foot-9 QB rising as a Heisman Trophy finalist before losing to Indiana’s Fernando Mendoza. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Curtis arrived as a prized five-star signing for Lea and the Commodores. He became the first-ever five-star addition in the era of College Football Recruiting rankings. Curtis’s addition showed that Vanderbilt has grown popular among recruits in recent years, especially through Lea’s coaching. The big 6-foot-4 passer has flashed his potential; completing 63% of his throws while throwing four touchdowns. Curtis also has tossed three interceptions while starting in the last two games. Curtis does bring his own mobility too, adding 133 yards on 41 carries. But now once again, Georgia and head coach Kirby Smart may need to prepare for a second quarterback ahead of Saturday. Blaze Berlowitz could receive the nod here if Curtis can’t go. He’s a senior and shares a previous New Mexico State connection with Pavia. Berlowitz has tossed 178 yards so far this season. So a Vanderbilt upset could come with a different QB behind center. But such a feat would become the second-biggest win in program history. home.headline: Penn State week 5 injury report vs. Northwestern: Who’s in, who’s out, and who has to step up
home.blurb: It’s still early in the year, but the injury bug has already bitten Penn State hard, forcing star wide receiver Koby Howard to miss the start of conference play. Howard’s absence was significant in the Nittany Lions Week 4 loss to Wisconsin, and he’ll be out again on Friday night when Matt Campbell’s team helps open the newly rebuilt Ryan Field at Northwestern. Daryus Dixson still listed as questionable on Thursday night availability report Dixson did not leave the Week 4 loss to the Badgers, but according to Campbell, who addressed Dixson’s health on Wednesday, he was “dinged up” just before halftime. Dixson was on the initial injury report on Tuesday night, listed as “questionable,” and held the same status on Thursday night when the availability report was released about 24 hours before kickoff in Evanston. The return of Alex Tatsch, who missed Week 1 as he ramped up from an injury he suffered preparing for the Pinstripe Bowl in December, has helped to fill the void left by Smith and Kooper Ebel, and Tony Rojas has been rock-solid at the second level of D’Anton Lynn’s defense. Dixson is seemingly the only player on Penn State’s roster whose status is uncertain heading into Friday night. Considering he played through the injury in the second half against Wisconsin, his outlook appears favorable, but that he wasn’t upgraded to “probable” raises a legitimate question about whether or not he’ll be ready to suit up against the Wildcats. Notable Northwestern injuries: Luke Dehnicke still doubtful While not ruled out, Northwestern has two starters listed as doubtful for Friday night, including its second-leading receiver: tight end Luke Dehnicke. home.blurb: Dehnicke, Eligon, Turner and Walters are all listed as questionable, while Fussell is doubtful for Friday's matchup. The biggest offensive name to watch may be Dehnicke. He has quickly developed a connection with quarterback Aidan Chiles and has become an important part of Chip Kelly's passing attack. Having him available against Penn State would give Chiles one of his most reliable targets as Northwestern looks to build off its 23-point performance against Indiana . The wide receiver has been dealing with a lower-body injury since Northwestern's season opener against South Dakota State and has missed the Wildcats' last two games. He is now listed as questionable, potentially giving Northwestern a chance to get another offensive weapon back for Friday night. The concerns are not limited to the offense. Turner is questionable after missing the Indiana game, while Fussell is doubtful after suffering an injury against the Hoosiers. Losing both would be a major concern for Northwestern's secondary against Penn State. With Oratokhai already out for the year , Northwestern will be hoping the availability report becomes more positive as Friday approaches. There is still time for that to happen. Under the Big Ten's availability reporting policy, teams release reports three days, two days and one day before conference games before submitting a final report two hours before kickoff. That means the status of Northwestern's questionable players could change throughout the week. Now, the Wildcats will hope to have as many of those pieces available as possible for another difficult Big Ten matchup. Northwestern hosts Penn State at 7 p.m. CT Friday on FOX, officially beginning a new era at Ryan Field.
